[[Carmichael Arena]] ([[2010 National Invitation Tournament|2010 NIT]]) |champion= |bowl=[[2010 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |bowl_result= Runner-Up }} {{2009–10 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. Their head coach was [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]]. The team played their home games in the [[Dean Smith Center]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], and were a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They were the defending National Champions. This was the 100th season of basketball in the school's history. The Tar Heels finished the season 20–17, 5–11 in ACC play, and lost in the first round of the [[2010 ACC men's basketball tournament]]. They received an invitation to the [[2010 National Invitation Tournament]], where they advanced to the championship game before falling to [[2009–10 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Dayton]]. == Preseason == The Tar Heels lost four starters from their [[2008–09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2008–09 Championship team]] and top backcourt reserve [[Bobby Frasor]]. [[Tyler Hansbrough]], the Atlantic Coast Conference all-time leading scorer, was selected in the lottery of the [[2009 NBA draft]], going #13 to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] [[Ty Lawson]] and [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]] [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] [[Wayne Ellington]] also were drafted in the first round, by the [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], respectively. Senior swingman [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]] was also drafted by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the second round. Top returnees were senior center [[Deon Thompson]], who spent the summer helping lead Team USA to a bronze at the [[World University Games]][http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/071109aac.html Thompson, USA Win Bronze Medal At World University Games] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090917025231/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/071109aac.html |date=2009-09-17 }} ''tarheelblue.com.'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. and sophomore [[Ed Davis (basketball)|Ed Davis]], who had been projected as a first-round draft pick. Reserve sophomores [[Larry Drew II]] and [[Tyler Zeller]] also returned, and junior swingman [[Will Graves]] was reinstated over the summer after a mid-season suspension by coach Roy Williams. Also returning was defensive stopper [[Marcus Ginyard]], who took a medical redshirt for the 2008–09 campaign after starting as a junior for the [[2007–08 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2007–08 Tar Heel team]], who advanced to the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]]. Joining the returnees was a recruiting class containing four [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-Americans]] and ranked as one of the top 5 in the nation.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120904024753/http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/northcarolina/story/70598.html|title=Heels ride their recruits}} ''Raleigh News and Observer'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. Despite the heavy losses for the defending champions, the Tar Heels were ranked in the top ten of both preseason polls when they were released on October 29,[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings 2010 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings – Preseason] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. even garnering a single vote for #1 in both the [[AP Poll]] and the [[Coaches Poll]]. UNC was ranked #6 in the AP and #4 in the Coaches Poll. The Tar Heels were also picked as the ACC pre-season favorite (with rival [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]) by the conference media, while Davis was chosen as a member of the preseason All-ACC Team.[http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102509aab.html Media Splits Top Spot in 2009–10 ACC Preseason Poll] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308100008/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102509aab.html |date=2012-03-08 }} ''Atlantic Coast Conference'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. Other preseason honors for Tar Heel players included the inclusion of Davis and Thompson on the 50-man [[Wooden Award]] preseason candidate list. Davis was also one of the 50 players named to the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]] watch list.[http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102909aaa.html Nine ACC Players Highlight Preseason Naismith List] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404184553/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102909aaa.html |date=2012-04-04 }} ''Atlantic Coast Conference'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. Marcus Ginyard was named a preseason candidate for the [[Lowe's Senior CLASS Award]], one of only two ACC players named to the 30-man list (with Duke's [[Jon Scheyer]]).[http://www.seniorclassaward.com/news/view/lowes_senior_class_award_names_2009-10_mens_and_womens_basketball_candidate/ Lowe’s Senior CLASS Award Names 2009–10 Men’s and Women’s Basketball Candidates] ''Lowe's Senior CLASS Award'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. ===100th anniversary celebration=== UNC kicked off their 100th season with an alumni game on September 4, featuring NBA players [[Vince Carter]], [[Antawn Jamison]] and [[Marvin Williams]]. At halftime, the 2009 National Championship banner was unveiled, and UNC legend [[Michael Jordan]] was honored for his election to the [[Basketball Hall of Fame]].[http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/090409abz.html Tar Heels Start 100th Season With Pro-Alumni Game] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091208073258/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/090409abz.html |date=2009-12-08 }} ''tarheelblue.com'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. The event proved to be an excellent recruiting tool for UNC, as 2011 forward prospect James McAdoo committed to North Carolina at the event, and [[Harrison Barnes]], the 2010 #1 recruit in the [[ESPNU]] and [[Scout.com]] rankings, later commited to UNC after attending the event. Members of the 2009 championship team received their championship rings at halftime of the UNC-[[The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina|Citadel]] football game on September 5. In their season opener against [[FIU Golden Panthers|Florida International]], the Tar Heels donned throwback uniforms in the style of the 1957 undefeated national championship team, with distinctive red trim.[https://www.sportingnews.com/college-basketball/article/2009-11-09/tar-heels-open-season-57-throwback-uniforms Tar Heels open season in '57 throwback uniforms] ''The Sporting News'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. They wore the 1957 throwback uniforms again when they played [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] on December 28. ===Recruiting=== Coach Roy Williams signed a five-person class for 2009, including two-time Tennessee Division II-AA [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball Award|Mr. Basketball]] Leslie McDonald from Memphis, identical twins [[David Wear|David]] and [[Travis Wear]] from California, and athletic combo guard Dexter Strickland from New Jersey. The crown jewel of the class was 6'10 forward [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]] of Tampa, Florida, rated the #1 PF by [[Scout.com]]. Henson, Strickland and the Wear twins were all named to the McDonald's game in Miami. Henson and Strickland were also named first-team ''[[Parade Magazine|Parade]]'' All-Americans, while McDonald and the Wears were called to the fourth team by the magazine.[http://www.parade.com/news/2009/04/parade-all-america-high-school-boys-basketball-team.html Meet Parade's All-America High School Boys Basketball Team] ''Parade Magazine'' Retrieved on season=== UNC kicked off their non-conference schedule on November 9 against Florida International and new coach [[Isiah Thomas]] as a part of the [[Coaches Vs. Cancer Classic]], defeating the Golden Panthers 88–72 at the [[Dean Smith Center]]. There had been some controversy surrounding the game, as FIU had threatened to pull out of the tournament when the brackets were released, and they found that they were not scheduled to play [[2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] as they had initially planned.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4422145 FIU wants to open versus Ohio State] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on November 14, 2009. After home wins over [[North Carolina Central Eagles|North Carolina Central]] and [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]], the Tar Heels began a tough out-of-conference slate which included five teams ranked in the preseason Coaches Poll. First was a trip to [[Madison Square Garden]] for the finals of the Coaches Vs. Cancer Classic. After defeating #15 Ohio State 77–73 in their semifinal game, the Tar Heels lost the championship game 87–71 to #24 [[2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]]. UNC had a two-point lead at the half, but the Orange used a 25–3 run coming out of the locker room to defeat the young Tar Heels convincingly behind 25 points from forwarding [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wesley Johnson]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20091124043216/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293240153 Thompson, Zeller help Tar Heels bounce back from first loss] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on November 23, 2009. In a 93–72 home win over [[Gardner-Webb Runnin' Bulldogs|Gardner-Webb]] on November 23, 2009, senior Deon Thompson became the 63rd player in UNC history to score 1,000 points. The milestone capped a 22-point, 10-rebound performance from Thompson. Gardner-Webb guard Grayson Flittner also tied a [[Dean Smith Center]] record with nine three-pointers.[https://web.archive.org/web/20091128061353/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293270153 Syracuse opens second half with 22–1 run to topple North Carolina] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on November 21, 2009. In their next game it was [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams']] turn to achieve a milestone, as he won his 600th game in the Tar Heels' 80–73 win over [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120720064926/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293330153|title=No. 11 North Carolina 80, Nevada 73}} ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on November 29, 2009. Next up was #9 [[2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in Chapel Hill as a part of the [[ACC – Big Ten Challenge]]. In this rematch of the 2009 NCAA title game, they again beat the Spartans 89–82 behind Ed Davis' 22 points and Larry Drew II's 18 points and six assists. The next game got no more comfortable, as UNC traveled to [[Rupp Arena]] to face the #5 [[2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]]. The Tar Heels fell behind early as UK freshman [[John Wall]] sparked a 28–2 first-half run that punctuated a 15-point halftime deficit. The Tar Heels battled back to make the game close in the second half, but ultimately lost 68–66.[https://web.archive.org/web/20091208024935/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293390096 Kentucky freshman finishes off Tar Heels with late free throws] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on December 6, 2009. Following the Kentucky game, UNC defeated [[Presbyterian Blue Hose|Presbyterian]] 103–64 at the Smith Center before traveling to [[Cowboys Stadium]] in [[Dallas]] to take on the #2 ranked [[2009–10 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]] in the first basketball game played at that venue. The Longhorns defeated the Tar Heels 103–90 behind [[Damion James]]' 25 points and 15 rebounds. Ed Davis had 21 points and nine rebounds in the loss.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120715132307/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293530251|title=James leads four with at least 20 points in an offensive shootout over UNC}} ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on December 29, 2009. The Tar Heels bounced back with home wins over [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]] (98–61) and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] (81–67). The Carolina front line of Davis, Thompson, Graves, and Zeller combined for 64 points and 30 rebounds in the win over Marshall, while freshman Dexter Strickland notched 18 in the win over Rutgers in the absence of Marcus Ginyard, who sat out the game with an ankle sprain. Ginyard also missed the last two non-conference games. In a home contest against [[Albany Great Danes men's basketball|Albany]], UNC lost junior forward Will Graves to an ankle injury. The Tar Heels won the game, 87–70, but lost both Graves and reserve Justin Watts for their last non-conference game at the [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]]. The Tar Heels played a real road game at [[Carolina First Arena]], down two starters. Charleston's Cougars played the Heels shot for shot, sending the game into overtime with an Andrew Goudelock three-pointer. In overtime, the Cougars outscored the Tar Heels to take the game 82–79 in a big upset. Ed Davis had 19 points, 16 rebounds and five blocks in the losing effort.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100112132624/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300040232 Goudelock's three ties game with 2 seconds in regulation, Cougars win in OT] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on January 11, 2010. ===Conference season=== The Tar Heels entered conference play by hosting the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]]. The Tar Heels returned injured starters, Will Graves and Marcus Ginyard, while the Hokies welcomed back their star [[Malcolm Delaney]]. Delaney lived up to his preseason All-ACC billing, scoring 20 points in the first half as Virginia Tech led 38–34 at the intermission. [[Larry Drew II]], Will Graves and Ed Davis led a strong second half effort to take the Tar Heels to a 78–64 win.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100115165212/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300100153 No. 9 North Carolina uses second-half burst to top Virginia Tech] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on January 11, 2010. The next three games were not as positive for the Tar Heels. They were beaten convincingly by [[2009–10 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] 83–64 in a game that saw UNC commit 26 turnovers. The Tar Heels showed signs of life in their next match against [[2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]]. After trailing the Yellow Jackets by as much as 20, UNC came storming back to take the lead with under a minute to play, behind Will Graves' 24 points. However, Georgia Tech scored the last three aspects of the game to get the win.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100120031257/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300160153 Peacock's shot caps win for Yellow Jackets; Shumpert has career-high 30] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on January 17, 2010. The Tar Heels looked to get back to their winning ways against Wake Forest at home, but were outscored in both halves, losing 82–69. This was the first time Roy Williams had lost three games in a row as Tar Heels head coach.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100122190623/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300200153 Harris has career day as Wake hands UNC first 3-game skid under Williams] ''ESPN.com'' Retrieved on January 24, 2010. The loss knocked the Tar Heels out of the national rankings for the first time since 2006. The Tar Heels were not able to achieve any real consistency for the remainder of the season, going only 4–8 for the rest of the way. While they did manage to sweep rival [[North Carolina State Wolfpack|North Carolina State]], they were swept by [[Duke Blue Devils|Duke]], including an 82–50 flogging to close the season. They finished 5–11 in conference play—only the fourth losing ACC record UNC has ever suffered, and easily the worst conference record in Williams' 22 years as a head coach. They also finished tied for ninth in the conference standings, their third-ever finish below fourth in ACC play. The Tar Heels briefly showed signs of life in the first half of the [[2010 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] against Georgia Tech, gaining an early lead, but a second-half swoon resulted in a 62–58 loss. ===Postseason=== The Tar Heels were left out of the 2010 NCAA Tournament, becoming the first defending national champion since [[2007–08 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]'s 2007–08 unit to not make the next year's tournament while eligible to compete. They were, however, selected for the [[2010 National Invitation Tournament]], their first appearance in that tourney since 2003. Despite a 16–16 record, the Tar Heels were a #4 seed, allowing them to host a first-round game against [[William & Mary Tribe|William & Mary]]. The game was played in the Tar Heels' former home, [[Carmichael Arena]], due to renovations at the Smith Center. After defeating William & Mary, the Tar Heels won road games at [[2009–10 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] and [[2009–10 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] and advanced to the tournament's semi-finals in [[Madison Square Garden]] where they defeated [[University of Rhode Island|Rhode Island]] in overtime. In the NIT championship game, they lost to Dayton 79–68 to close the season at 20–17. The 17 losses were the second-most in school history. On April 1, [[Deon Thompson]] appeared in the [[2010 NIT#NIT Final Four - NIT Semifinals and NIT Championship Game|NIT Championship game]], giving him 152 career game appearances.{{cite web | title = UNC's Thompson will set mark in final game | publisher = North Carolina News Observer | date = April 1, 2010 | url = http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/03/31/415977/uncs-thompson-will-set-mark-in.html | access-date = April 1, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100404104800/http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/03/31/415977/uncs-thompson-will-set-mark-in.html| archive-date= 4 April 2010 | url-status= live}} This set the [[NCAA]] all-time career games played mark, formerly held by [[Wayne Turner (basketball)|Wayne Turner]] of [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Walter Hodge]] of [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. ==Roster== {{CBB roster/Header|year=2009|team=North Carolina Tar Heels|teamcolors=y|high_school=yes}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Marc|last=Campbell|num=2|pos=G|ft=5|in=11|lbs=175|class=SR|rs=|home=[[Raleigh, North Carolina|Raleigh, NC]]|high_school=[[Ravenscroft School|Ravenscroft]]}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Ed|last=Davis|alt=Ed Davis (basketball)|link=y||num=32|pos=F|ft=6|in=10|lbs=220|class=SO|rs=|home=[[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond, VA]]|high_school=[[Benedictine High School (Richmond, Virginia)|Benedictine]]}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Larry|last=Drew II|link=y|num=11|pos=G|ft=6|in=1|lbs=180|class=SO|rs=|home=[[Encino, Los Angeles, California|Encino, CA]]|high_school=[[William Howard Taft High School (Los Angeles)|Woodland Hills Taft]]}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Marcus|last=Ginyard|link=y|num=1|pos=G|ft=6|in=5|lbs=210|class=SR|rs=y|home=[[Alexandria, Virginia|Alexandria, VA]]|high_school=[[Bishop Denis J.
